clue.text: Crooked cop able to identify fake pill

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of true, so the letters that follow are twisted into another order

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dishonest policeman manages to spot a counterfeit tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy medication with no active ingredient, given for its psychological effect.

clue.text: Enthusiasm of up and coming salesman for spice

parts.note: pep is energy or enthusiasm

indicators.note: in a down entry, something coming up is read from the bottom, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: An ambitious young salesman's keenness for selling spices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up and coming' looks like praise for the salesman, but it tells you to write his abbreviation upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepper is the pungent ground berry used as a seasoning, a standard example of a spice.

clue.text: Rob from boat train on the way up to reach one's goal

indicators.note: going up a down entry means reading the word from its end, so it runs backwards
taking something from a phrase means those letters are removed from it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; the letters to be removed come out of it

explanation.surface: A thief robs passengers on a boat train heading towards their destination.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove B, O and R, in that order, from BOATTRAIN: the B and O of boat go, then the R of train, leaving AT + TAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain is to achieve or arrive at an aim, exactly what reaching one's goal means.

clue.text: Silver-tongued Liberal unknown speaks in a spell-binding way

parts.note: silver-tongued means fluent and persuasive
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking Liberal no one has heard of gives a mesmerising speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking eloquently means with fluent, moving expression, the manner that holds an audience spellbound.

clue.text: Bizarre route in need of repair

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so its letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A road so badly maintained that it has become strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré is a French borrowing meaning unconventional or eccentric, a close synonym of strange and weird.

clue.text: Music coming from the French boat first

indicators.note: first says the vessel is placed at the front, ahead of the French word

parts.note: a skiff is a small light rowing boat
le is French for 'the' (masculine)

explanation.surface: Tunes drifting from a French boat that leads the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue mentions 'the French' before 'boat', but 'first' puts the boat at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiffle is a 1950s style of folk-influenced popular music played on homemade instruments like washboards.

clue.text: Wastes new day inside square's compound

indicators.note: inside tells us two short pieces sit within the longer word
a compound is a mixture, so the combined letters are mixed up

parts.note: the possessive 's read as a plain S
N is the abbreviation for new
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A new day is wasted inside the walls of a town square's compound.
explanation.walkthrough: N and D go inside SQUARES to make SQUA(ND)RES, and those nine letters are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To squander is to spend money or time recklessly, so squanders is a verb synonym of wastes.

clue.text: Gen to illuminate notes Foreign Office initially assembled

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word in the run

parts.note: the leading letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Intelligence gathered to brief the Foreign Office on its notes.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information, as in 'what's the gen?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both info and gen are informal clipped words for facts or information.

clue.text: Just tolerable drama

definitions.note: adjective for the noun phrase; 'fair play' here stands for what is just

parts.note: fair can mean moderately good, passable
a play is a stage drama

explanation.surface: A theatre critic's verdict: only passable drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' reads as 'merely', but it is the definition, meaning fair or right.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair play means honest, even-handed treatment, the quality of being just.

clue.text: Somehow need to protect breach before being overwhelmed

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other
somehow suggests an unspecified rearrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
a gulf is a gap or rift

explanation.surface: Someone must defend a breach in the wall before being overrun.
explanation.definitionFit: Engulfed means swamped or swallowed up, as by a flood, so it matches overwhelmed.

clue.text: Play a tune in observatory initially, then on terrace

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word before it

parts.note: the leading letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Someone plays music in an observatory and then out on the terrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor area next to a house, much the same thing as a terrace.

clue.text: Spoiled turf to throw when collecting fungi

indicators.note: spoiled means messed up, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
to fling is to throw

explanation.surface: A pig churns up the lawn while foraging for mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Truffles are prized underground fungi, traditionally sniffed out by pigs that root up the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Truffling is hunting for truffles, which are fungi, so it means gathering fungi.

clue.text: Bon vivants are an infamously supine race

indicators.note: acting infamously means behaving badly, so the letters are misbehaving out of order

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A jibe that pleasure-seekers are a notoriously lazy breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicureans are people devoted to fine food and pleasure, which is what bon vivants are.

clue.text: Jewel in ring father left

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
pa is an informal word for father
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A gemstone set in a ring that Dad bequeathed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is an iridescent gemstone, an example of a jewel.

clue.text: Crustacean able to trap flies?

parts.note: surface reading: an odd shellfish that catches insects
setter's reading: the eight-legged web-spinner that catches flies names the first word of this crustacean

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about a shellfish that catches insects.
explanation.walkthrough: The trapper of flies is the arachnid that gives this long-legged crab its name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sea crab with long thin legs and a small body, named for its arachnid-like look.

clue.text: Unfeeling prelate dealt with vehicle identification

parts.note: numb means without sensation

indicators.note: cards that are dealt get shuffled first, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A heartless bishop handled a car registration matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The split falls after NUMB, not after NUMBER, so all seven letters of prelate are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A number plate is the sign on a car bearing its registration, which identifies the vehicle.

clue.text: Note two alluding to American author

parts.note: to mark is to note or notice
twain is an old word for two

explanation.surface: A footnote referring twice to an American writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain is the pen name of Samuel Clemens, author of Huckleberry Finn, a famous American author.

clue.text: Sailor, to a great extent badly bred, becomes engaged

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: badly suggests the word is mangled, so its letters come out disordered

parts.note: so means very much, as in 'so tired'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rough-mannered sailor somehow gets betrothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' tempts as getting married; here it means fully occupied in something.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbed means engrossed or occupied, the sense of being engaged in a task.

clue.text: Dainty, unusual set that's most delightful

parts.note: sweet can mean pretty and delicate

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the word is not in its ordinary order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A delicate, unusual tea set is the most charming of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetest is the superlative of sweet in its sense of pleasing or charming.

clue.text: Censored bowlers died tragically

indicators.note: tragically suggests disaster, and the letters are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A news report about bowlers who died tragically is cut by the censor.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Bowdler published an expurgated Shakespeare, giving his name to cutting out offensive material.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowdlerise a text is to remove passages thought improper, which is a form of censorship.

clue.text: Hero in audition after sundown

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: the period after sunset

explanation.surface: An actor auditions for the hero's part in an evening show.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight is a chivalrous warrior of romance, the type of a hero.

clue.text: Facet of dreadful spa using shock therapy

indicators.note: dreadful means terribly bad, so the following word is badly jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: One feature of an awful health spa is its use of electric shock treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is one side or feature of something, the same as a facet.

clue.text: Poems of almost all styles

indicators.note: almost all means one short of the whole, so a single letter is dropped

parts.note: modes are styles or manners

explanation.surface: Verses written in nearly every possible form.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually the dropped letter is the first, M, not the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems addressed to a subject, so they are an example of poems.

clue.text: Gypsies' move set in train

indicators.note: a move shifts things about, so these letters change position

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Travellers have begun the process of moving on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set in train' means started; the apostrophe on Gypsies' is surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerants are people who travel from place to place, a wider term covering travelling Gypsies.

clue.text: Negative church score

parts.note: not expresses negation
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A church choir gets a bad mark for its music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like music or points; here it is a verb or noun meaning a cut mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a V-shaped cut, and to score means to mark with a cut line.

clue.text: Lady's fingers drawn by fine artist

parts.note: OK means fine or all right
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A woman's hands sketched by a skilled painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady's fingers is the British name for okra; 'drawn by' sounds like sketching but only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra pods are long and tapering, which is why the vegetable is also called lady's fingers.

clue.text: Secured, after pause for a meal

indicators.note: after says the first-named word follows the second in the answer

parts.note: a break is a pause
fast means firmly fixed

explanation.surface: Everything tied down, the crew stop for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast is the first meal of the day, literally breaking the overnight fast.

clue.text: Villain's gore spilled around university

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other
spilled means scattered about, so these letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A villain's victim's blood is spattered across a campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or unprincipled person, a synonym of villain.

clue.text: Journalist recalled retinue had to get off at a station

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word goes back to front

parts.note: ED, editor, is a journalist
a train is a body of attendants

explanation.surface: A reporter is called back from a trip, and the whole entourage has to leave the train.
explanation.definitionFit: To detrain is to alight from a railway carriage, which one does at a station.

clue.text: Dress at one's home ground

parts.note: a habit is a monk's or nun's robe
taken as written

explanation.surface: How one dresses on familiar territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural environment where a creature lives, its home territory.
